name: Meta AI
summary: The lab that made open weights a frontier strategy. Llama was not the first model anyone could download, but it was the first one worth downloading, and most of the open ecosystem dates itself from that release. Meta publishes weights and licences freely, and benchmark methodology sparingly.

founders.name: Yann LeCun
founders.bio: Turing Award laureate for convolutional networks; set up Facebook AI Research in 2013 and shaped its open-publication stance.

founders.name: Mark Zuckerberg
founders.bio: Chose to release Llama weights publicly, the decision most of the open-weights field is downstream of.

name: Mistral AI
summary: Europe's answer to the American frontier labs, founded by three researchers out of DeepMind and Meta. Ships an unusually clean split — small open-weight models anyone can run, larger commercial ones behind an API — and says plainly which is which.

founders.name: Arthur Mensch
founders.bio: Former DeepMind researcher; worked on the Chinchilla scaling results that reset how the field sizes models against data.

founders.name: Guillaume Lample
founders.bio: Led the original Llama work at Meta before leaving to start Mistral.

founders.name: Timothée Lacroix
founders.bio: Also from the Meta Llama team; owns Mistral's training and inference stack.

name: DeepSeek
summary: Spun out of a quantitative hedge fund, and the lab that proved a frontier-class reasoning model could be trained for a fraction of the assumed cost and then given away. Publishes unusually detailed training papers alongside the weights, which makes its numbers easier to check than most.

founders.name: Liang Wenfeng
founders.bio: Co-founder of the quant fund High-Flyer; funded DeepSeek from its GPU cluster and kept the weights open.

name: Qwen
summary: Alibaba Cloud's model family, and the most prolific release schedule in the field by a wide margin — base, instruct, coder, math, vision and audio variants at half a dozen sizes each. Nearly all of it is open weights, which is why so much of the fine-tuned long tail starts here.

founders.name: Alibaba Cloud
founders.bio: Alibaba's cloud arm; the Qwen team sits inside it and ships under the Tongyi brand in China.

name: xAI
summary: Built a frontier training cluster faster than anyone expected and put the resulting models straight into X. Publishes benchmark numbers in launch posts and very little else, so almost everything here is sourced to an announcement rather than to documentation.

founders.name: Elon Musk
founders.bio: Co-founded OpenAI in 2015, left its board in 2018, and started xAI in 2023.

name: Microsoft AI
summary: Two things under one name: Microsoft Research, which has published the small Phi models for years, and the Microsoft AI division formed in 2024 to build first-party frontier models rather than only resell OpenAI's. The Phi line is the part with open weights and reproducible numbers.

founders.name: Mustafa Suleyman
founders.bio: Co-founded DeepMind and then Inflection AI; joined Microsoft in 2024 with most of Inflection's team.

name: Amazon AGI
summary: The Nova family, built to be the default on Bedrock rather than to top a leaderboard. Amazon competes on price and on already being integrated with the rest of AWS, and its published benchmark coverage is thinner than its pricing detail.

founders.name: Rohit Prasad
founders.bio: Formerly head scientist for Alexa; leads the group that ships the Nova models.

name: NVIDIA
summary: Sells the hardware every other lab here trains on, and also ships its own open models — Nemotron, and a long line of speech and vision work. Its releases exist partly to demonstrate what its chips do, which is worth knowing when reading its benchmark numbers.

founders.name: Jensen Huang
founders.bio: Has run NVIDIA since 1993; made the bet on CUDA that turned a graphics company into the substrate of the field.

founders.name: Chris Malachowsky
founders.bio: Engineering co-founder; still with the company as an NVIDIA Fellow.

founders.name: Curtis Priem
founders.bio: Designed NVIDIA's first graphics architecture.

name: Cohere
summary: Built for enterprises rather than consumers — retrieval, embeddings, and models that can be deployed inside a customer's own environment. Its research arm, Cohere Labs, publishes the Aya multilingual work openly.

founders.name: Aidan Gomez
founders.bio: A co-author of "Attention Is All You Need", the paper the entire transformer era rests on.

founders.name: Nick Frosst
founders.bio: First employee of Geoffrey Hinton's Google Brain group in Toronto.

founders.name: Ivan Zhang
founders.bio: Leads Cohere's applied research and product engineering.

name: Allen Institute for AI
summary: A non-profit, and the only lab here that releases the training data alongside the weights. OLMo and Molmo exist to be reproduced rather than to win, which makes Ai2 the reference point for what "open" is supposed to mean in this field.

founders.name: Paul Allen
founders.bio: Co-founder of Microsoft; endowed the institute in 2014 to do AI research outside the commercial race.

founders.name: Oren Etzioni
founders.bio: Set the institute's open-by-default publication stance.

name: Moonshot AI
summary: Makes Kimi, and got there by going long on context before most of the field did. The recent Kimi releases are open weights at a scale that used to be closed, and they are trained explicitly for agentic tool use rather than for chat.

founders.name: Yang Zhilin
founders.bio: Co-author of Transformer-XL and XLNet, both long-context results, which is visible in what Moonshot ships.

name: Z.ai
summary: Spun out of Tsinghua University as Zhipu AI and now trading as Z.ai. The GLM family is open weights across text, vision and code, and the lab publishes its evaluation setups in more detail than most of its peers.

founders.name: Tang Jie
founders.bio: Tsinghua professor; led the GLM pre-training work the company was founded on.

founders.name: Li Juanzi
founders.bio: Tsinghua professor of knowledge engineering, co-founder of the Zhipu spin-out.

name: MiniMax
summary: Ships across text, speech, music and video from one house, which almost nobody outside the largest labs does. Its text models lean on linear-attention variants to push context length rather than on more parameters.

founders.name: Yan Junjie
founders.bio: Former vice-president at SenseTime; founded MiniMax in 2021.

name: Perplexity
summary: An answer engine first and a lab second, but it does train and release its own models — the Sonar line, and open post-trained variants of other labs' weights. Every answer it gives carries citations, which is the one idea this site and that product share.

founders.name: Aravind Srinivas
founders.bio: Former research scientist at OpenAI; founded Perplexity in 2022.

founders.name: Denis Yarats
founders.bio: Previously a research scientist at Meta AI.

founders.name: Johnny Ho
founders.bio: Leads Perplexity's search and indexing systems.

founders.name: Andy Konwinski
founders.bio: Co-founded Databricks before Perplexity.

name: Inflection AI
summary: Built Pi and the Inflection models, then lost most of its team to Microsoft in 2024 and turned to enterprise deployment. Kept here because the models it shipped are part of the record, not because it is still setting the frontier.

founders.name: Mustafa Suleyman
founders.bio: Co-founded DeepMind, then Inflection; left for Microsoft AI in 2024.

founders.name: Reid Hoffman
founders.bio: Co-founder of LinkedIn and a longtime backer of both DeepMind and OpenAI.

founders.name: Karén Simonyan
founders.bio: Led deep learning scaling at DeepMind; now chief scientist at Microsoft AI.

name: Baidu
summary: Shipped ERNIE Bot in March 2023, the first large Chinese chatbot to reach the public, and has kept the ERNIE line running since. Recent releases are open weights; the earlier ones were only ever available through Baidu's own cloud.

founders.name: Robin Li
founders.bio: Invented the RankDex link-analysis method before founding Baidu in 2000.

founders.name: Eric Xu
founders.bio: Co-founded Baidu and served as its chairman.
